info.title: Galaxy Explorer API
info.description: REST API for building and exploring galaxies. Bodies are JSON in camelCase, wrapped as `{ "data": … }`; lists add `nextCursor`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json. Every write is one change batch (X-GE-Batch-Id in the response), which can be reverted. Updates need the `version` you read. Conventions: docs/plan/architecture.md §5.

get.description: A celestial object: a system, star, planet, moon, asteroid belt, station, nebula, anomaly, black hole or marker (`baseType`). Objects nest: `parentId` is the object it sits inside, or null for the top level of the galaxy. Which parents a base type allows is fixed (a planet goes in a system or the galaxy; a moon in a planet). x, y, z are a position in the parent's frame: light-years in the galaxy (+Y is galactic north), system units (roughly AU) inside a system, and body radii around a planet. `explorable` makes systems open a system view and planets or moons an orbit view. `appearance` holds only overrides of the type and subtype defaults.

post.summary: Run many operations as one change
post.description:
Runs up to 1000 operations in order, in one transaction and one change batch: all of them happen, or none do, and the whole request is one undo step.

Operations: create, update, delete and upsert for any entity kind (`kind` is celestial_object, group, place, event or character; `data` is the same body as that kind's single-resource route), and setLocation, addMembers, removeMembers, setFacts, addLink and addRelation on an entity `id`.

Refer to an entity created earlier in the same request as `"$op:N"` (N counts from 0), anywhere an id goes. For example, create a system, then planets with `"parentId": "$op:0"`.

If an operation fails, nothing is written, and the problem response's `operationIndex` names it. With `dryRun: true` everything runs and is reported, including `impact` (rows touched per table), and then rolled back; use it to preview deletes.

id.description: What "$op:N" stood for: the entity created or changed.

impact.description: Dry runs only: rows that would be inserted, updated and deleted, per table.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Is the API up, and can it reach its database?

tags.name: universes
tags.description: Fictional settings; everything else lives inside one.

tags.name: maps
tags.description: One galaxy at one point in time.

tags.name: objects
tags.description: A celestial object: a system, star, planet, moon, asteroid belt, station, nebula, anomaly, black hole or marker (`baseType`). Objects nest: `parentId` is the object it sits inside, or null for the top level of the galaxy. Which parents a base type allows is fixed (a planet goes in a system or the galaxy; a moon in a planet). x, y, z are a position in the parent's frame: light-years in the galaxy (+Y is galactic north), system units (roughly AU) inside a system, and body radii around a planet. `explorable` makes systems open a system view and planets or moons an orbit view. `appearance` holds only overrides of the type and subtype defaults.

tags.name: groups
tags.description: A named set of top-level objects drawn as a colored outline: a sector, territory or faction. Its `groupTypeId` (a universe setting) decides which layer it belongs to and how groups nest: a Sub-sector's `parentGroupId` must be a Sector. An object is in at most one group of each type. Members are managed under /groups/{id}/members. `outlineColor` defaults to the group type's color.

tags.name: places
tags.description: A lasting place, such as a city, fortress or ruin. Where it is lives in its location (PUT /entities/{id}/location): on a planet or moon at a latitude and longitude, at an object, at a position in space, or at another place.

tags.name: events
tags.description: Something that happened. `dateText` is free text in the universe's own date format (such as "240.M41"); `dateSort` is an optional number to order events by. It may have a location like a place, and characters relate to it with the `participant` relation.

tags.name: characters
tags.description: A person or being, shared by every map of the universe (characters belong to the universe, not to one map). Link a character to the events they took part in with the `participant` relation.

tags.name: group-types
tags.description: A kind of group in this universe, such as Segmentum, Sector or Sub-sector (T5). `layer` gathers types shown together (Administrative, Political). `parentGroupTypeId` makes types nest: groups of this type sit inside groups of the parent type.

tags.name: event-categories
tags.description: A category for events, with the icon and color of their pins, such as Battle or Discovery.

tags.name: object-subtypes
tags.description: A universe-specific refinement of an object base type, such as Hive World (a planet) or Webway Gate (an anomaly) (U2). `defaultAppearance` sits between the base type's defaults and each object's overrides.

tags.name: field-definitions
tags.description: A custom fact this universe records, such as Population or Tithe Grade (U2). Entities get values for it under /entities/{id}/facts. `valueType` is text, number, date_text or url. `appliesToKind` (and optionally a base type or subtype) says which entities it is for.

tags.name: images
tags.description: Uploaded images attached to an entity.

tags.name: links
tags.description: Web links attached to an entity.

tags.name: facts
tags.description: Values of the universe's custom fields, such as Population.

tags.name: relations
tags.description: How entities relate, such as a character involved in an event.

tags.name: locations
tags.description: Where a place or event is.

tags.name: batch
tags.description: Many operations in one transaction and one undo step.

tags.name: history
tags.description: Every change, what it did, and undo and redo.

tags.name: views
tags.description: Render-ready payloads for the galaxy, system and orbit views.
